land.text: Kelantan as it stood when transferred to British protection (the 1762 outline)

successors.note: 'Kelantan was transferred to British Protection on 19 July 1909' (Kelantan Sultanate page); Siam had been the suzerain, so the matching vassal_end (July 1909) is recorded here and in rattanakosin-kingdom. Cliopatria's Kelantan row stops in 1904.

capitals.name: Kota Lama (Kubang Labu area, old royal seat)
capitals.note: The page names the early seats (a raja 'at Kubang Labu' in 1760; Istana Kota Lama as the administrative centre until 1840) but gives no coordinates; the position is Kota Bharu's, which lies on the same lower Kelantan River.

capitals.name: Kota Bharu
capitals.note: Istana Balai Besar 'was constructed in 1840' and replaced Istana Kota Lama; the Kelantan page says Muhammad II's fort 'became Kota Bharu in 1844'. The two pages differ by four years.

correction.text: the territories reunited under a single ruler in 1760

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's Kelantan begins in 1762 but the page puts the unification of Kelantan's 'disparate territories under a single ruler' in 1760 (the Kelantan page: 'Around 1760, Long Yunus ... succeeded in unifying the territory'). The 1762 shape is carried back two years.

8,555 km2 against the infobox 15,040 km2 for the modern state (ratio 0.57, inside a factor of two); the shape is the lowland core and the pages give no inland frontier. Held 1762-1889 through the Terengganu episode (1795-1800) and the Siamese tributary status (1786 on the Kelantan infobox, 1812 on the Sultanate page), neither of which changes the shape (both are recorded as vassal_start 1786 and vassal_end July 1909 with rattanakosin-kingdom).

One cell (about 230 km2) fewer than the 1762 shape, bbox unchanged. Re-checked on the Kelantan, Kelantan Sultanate and Anglo-Siamese Treaty of 1909 pages: none mentions a boundary change, cession or loss in or around 1890 (the Sultanate page has only that Mansur 'Succeeded on his death, as Yang di-Pertuan in 1890'). With no page for the cause the loss event was dropped and the 1762 outline is carried instead.

region.text: the disparate territories of Kelantan under a single ruler

ledger.note: 1760: a raja reunites Kelantan's territories under a single ruler. The Sultanate page says the raja 'at Kubang Labu' (Long Muhammad or Long Pandak) 'succeeded in reuniting the disparate territories under a single ruler', overthrown 'four years later' by Long Yunus; the Kelantan page has 'Around 1760, Long Yunus ... succeeded in unifying the territory'. The pages differ on the man, not the date or the land.

1786: Kelantan comes under Siamese control. The Kelantan infobox gives 'Siamese control: 1786' and the article has no sentence describing the tributary status; the Kelantan Sultanate page dates the formal step later: Long Muhammad was 'installed as Raja and Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Kelantan on November 1801 and became a separate tributary of Siam in 1812'. The year 1786 is the infobox's; the region is the whole state. Mirrors rattanakosin-kingdom /ledger/7 (vassal_start 1786, counterpart kelantan).

region.text: the whole of Kelantan, whose control 'passed to Terengganu'

ledger.note: 1795: on Raja Yunus's death Terengganu takes control of Kelantan. 'Following the death of Raja Yunus in 1795, control of the state passed to Terengganu.' Tengku Muhammad, Terengganu's candidate, rules until 1800. The Kelantan page: Yunus was 'succeeded in 1795 by his son-in-law Tengku Muhammad'.

1800: Long Muhammad defeats the pro-Terengganu faction and rules Kelantan as Sultan Muhammad I. 'The pro-Terengganu faction was defeated in 1800 and Long Muhammad ruled Kelantan'; the Sultanate page: 'Defeated by Long Muhammad in 1800.' He was installed in November 1801 and 'accepted by the Siamese as ruler of a separate tributary, in 1812'.

1840: Sultan Muhammad II builds Istana Balai Besar, and the royal seat passes from Kota Lama to the new town of Kota Bharu ('was constructed in 1840'). The Kelantan page dates the fort that 'became Kota Bharu' to 1844.

July 1909: Siam's suzerainty over Kelantan ends. 'Kelantan was transferred to British Protection on 19 July 1909' (Kelantan Sultanate page). The Anglo-Siamese Treaty of 1909 page (signed 10 March 1909, ratifications exchanged in London 9 July 1909) has Siam transfer 'all rights of suzerainty, protection, administration and control' over Kelantan, Terengganu, Kedah and Perlis; this page's 19 July is kept for the dissolve. Mirrors rattanakosin-kingdom /ledger/40 (vassal_end 1909-07, counterpart kelantan).

region.text: Kelantan, transferred to British protection (the 1762 outline, carried through 1909)

ledger.note: 19 July 1909: Kelantan passes from Siamese suzerainty to British protection. 'Kelantan was transferred to British Protection on 19 July 1909'; 'Under the terms of the Anglo-Siamese Treaty of 1909, the Thais relinquished their claims over Kelantan' (Kelantan page, not the Sultanate page, which does not mention the treaty). The Anglo-Siamese Treaty page used by the rattanakosin-kingdom dossier gives 9 July (ratifications exchanged); this page's date is kept. Kelantan continues as an Unfederated Malay State and, from 1948, a state of Malaya.

wars.name: Kelantan succession struggle with Terengganu
wars.outcome: Terengganu's candidate Tengku Muhammad held Kelantan from Yunus's death in 1795; Long Muhammad defeated the pro-Terengganu faction in 1800 and ruled as Sultan Muhammad I.
wars.note: 'The pro-Terengganu faction was defeated in 1800 and Long Muhammad ruled Kelantan.' No battle or place is named on the pages; the zone is the whole state.

certainty.note: No page opened gives a surveyed or treaty frontier for Kelantan before the Anglo-Siamese Treaty of 1909; the Cliopatria outline is a lowland core. The Pattani and Terengganu frontiers are approximate throughout.

notes: Budget 1-2 pages: both used. Kelantan was a Siamese tributary from 1786 (Kelantan infobox 'Siamese control: 1786') or from 1812 as a separate tributary (Sultanate page); the vassal tint is recorded on both sides (repair of 2026-10-19): vassal_start 1786 and vassal_end July 1909 here, mirroring rattanakosin-kingdom /ledger/7 and /ledger/40. The 1795-1800 Terengganu control is recorded as a contest between the two (the sultanate-of-terengganu dossier is another agent's). Cliopatria's Kelantan row ends in 1904 while the page has the sovereignty ending on 19 July 1909; two new keyframes (1760-1761, 1905-1909) carry the outline to the page's dates. Repair of 2026-10-19: the 1890 one-cell loss (confidence 1, counterpart unknown) was dropped after the Kelantan, Kelantan Sultanate and Anglo-Siamese Treaty of 1909 pages named no boundary change; keyframes 1890, 1900 and 1905 now carry the 1762 outline. The 1795-1800 contest is not mirrored in sultanate-of-terengganu (se-03-a), which should carry contest_start 1795 and contest_end 1800 naming kelantan. Not settled: why Cliopatria stops in 1904; the page gives no inland (Ulu Kelantan) frontier, so the 8,555 km2 shape is 57 percent of the modern state's area. The Kelantan and Sultanate pages differ on who unified the territory around 1760 (Long Yunus versus Long Muhammad or Long Pandak) and on the date Kota Bharu was founded (1840 or 1844). No region names outside Natural Earth were used.
